record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Given an asymptotically flat initial data set (M, g, K) in mathematical relativity and a future trapped surface Sigma, must there exist a smooth spherical apparent horizon outside Sigma, and must there also exist an apparent horizon inside Sigma?

evidence.quote: Given an asymptotically flat (AF) initial data set (M,g,K) and a (future) trapped surface L (i.e. tr:E(K+k) ~ 0), (a) show there is a (smooth, spherical) apparent horizon outside 2:. (b) show there is an apparent horizon inside :E.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g,K)$ be an asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations, that is, $(M,g)$ is a complete 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold with one or more asymptotically Euclidean ends and $K$ is a symmetric (0,2)-tensor on $M$ representing the second fundamental form of $M$ in an ambient Lorentzian spacetime. For a closed orientable two-sided surface $\Sigma\subset M$ with outward unit normal $\nu$, denote by $H_\Sigma$ its mean curvature with respect to $\nu$ and by $\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$ the trace of $K$ restricted to $\Sigma$. The (future) outgoing null expansion is $\theta^+(\Sigma)=H_\Sigma+\mathrm{tr}_\Sigma K$, and $\Sigma$ is called a (future) trapped surface if $\theta^+(\Sigma)<0$ on $\Sigma$. A surface with $\theta^+=0$ is called a marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS); an apparent horizon is a smooth hypersurface in $M$ foliated by, or equal to, a MOTS (commonly the boundary of the region containing trapped surfaces).

Suppose $\Sigma\subset M$ is a (future) trapped surface in an asymptotically flat initial data set $(M,g,K)$.

(a) Must there exist a smooth apparent horizon (a smooth MOTS) lying outside $\Sigma$ (i.e., separating $\Sigma$ from the asymptotic end), and can it be taken to be of spherical topology?

(b) Must there also exist an apparent horizon lying inside $\Sigma$ (on the side opposite to the asymptotic end)?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of an outermost MOTS outside a given trapped surface in an asymptotically flat initial data set has been established by work of Andersson–Metzger and Eichmair (existence and regularity of outermost MOTS in dimensions ≤ 7), and the outermost MOTS is known to consist of components of spherical topology by results of Galloway and Schoen. However, the existence of an apparent horizon strictly inside a trapped surface (part (b)) is not generally established and remains a recognized open problem in mathematical relativity.

status_evidence.title: Construction of Cauchy data for the dynamical formation of apparent horizons and the Penrose Inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth AF Cauchy data without MOTS whose future evolution contains a trapped region bounded by an apparent horizon (smooth hypersurface foliated by MOTS).
status_evidence.claim: Apparent horizons can be characterized as smooth hypersurfaces foliated by MOTS; their existence in initial data depends on subtle conditions.

status_evidence.title: Scaling up the extrinsic curvature in asymptotically flat gravitational initial data: Generating trapped surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of MOTS, outermost MOTS and apparent horizons in AF initial data.
status_evidence.claim: Outermost MOTS exist outside any trapped surface in AF initial data sets, by results of Andersson-Metzger and Eichmair.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity (zbMATH)
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems including apparent horizon existence inside and outside a trapped surface.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of an apparent horizon inside a trapped surface is listed as open.
